title: Convert a Matrix to Upper Triangular
statement:
You are given a square matrix of `n` rows and `n` columns in which every element is non-zero. Convert it into an **upper triangular matrix**.

A square matrix is upper triangular when every element below the main diagonal is zero. Formally, for rows and columns numbered from `0`, every element at row `i` and column `j` with `i > j` must be `0`. The elements on the main diagonal (`i = j`) and above it (`i < j`) keep their original values.

Print the resulting matrix.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer `n`.
Each of the next `n` lines contains `n` integers, the elements of one row.
outputFormat: Print `n` lines of `n` space-separated integers: the upper triangular matrix.

examples.explanation: The elements 4, 7 and 8 lie below the main diagonal, so they become 0. Everything else is unchanged.
Only the element at row 1, column 0 is below the diagonal.
A 1 x 1 matrix has nothing below its diagonal.

hints: The main diagonal is where the row index equals the column index. Which comparison between i and j describes 'below' it?
Visit every cell once and replace it with 0 exactly when its row index is greater than its column index.
